title: Operatorless bootstrap choreography: terraform interfaces and non‑blocking upgrade safety
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working draft for an operatorless (minimal-operator) bootstrap choreography that works across mixed fleets: bare-metal (PXE/iPXE) + vSphere templated nodes. Focus is on: idempotent terraform module interfaces, non-blocking control-plane upgrades, observable health gates, and safe rollback paths.

Audience:
- Field deployment engineers
- Platform/infra SREs doing customer on-prem installs
- Solutions engineers customizing customer Terraform stacks

High-level approach (one paragraph):
We assume a small, deterministic bootstrap controller (not an in-cluster operator) that sequences node provisioning, image/firmware checks, and k8s control-plane joins. Terraform owns infra lifecycle (networks, VLANs, ESXi templates, PXE DHCP allocations), but it must expose a small, clear state interface so the controller can resume or re-run idempotently. Upgrades are staged: control-plane first (canary CP nodes), then kubelet/node reboots with local preflight, then optional workload cordon/drain. Telemetry and health gates run as pre- and post-step checks.

Design constraints / non‑goals:
- Non-goal: full-featured in-cluster operator lifecycle management.
- Constraint: some customer environments are air-gapped; all external calls must be optional and flag-driven.
- Constraint: minimal agent footprint on nodes until after join; prefer ephemeral init containers / cloud-init over persistent agents.

Terraform module interface notes (requirements for module authors):
- Module outputs must include: bootstrap_token_id, bootstrap_state_bucket (or s3 API-compatible URL), node_inventory_file (path or object id), and expected_control_plane_count.
- Modules must be idempotent: reapply should not delete annotated resources unless explicit flag set (e.g. terraform apply -var="purge=true").
- Provide an opt-in variable to toggle DHCP vs static IP provisioning for ipxe flows.
- Provide a minimal “resume token” object (small JSON blob) readable by the bootstrap controller in a stable storage location (S3, GCS, or customer NFS path).

Suggested small terraform module surface (pseudo-signature):
- variables: { cluster_name, region_tags, ipxe_enabled = true, vsphere_template = "rwi-k8s-node-v1", ssh_key_id, mtu_override = null, management_vlan_id, service_cidr }
- outputs: { bootstrap_token_id, resume_blob_uri, expected_control_plane_count, node_group_ids }

Idempotency patterns to follow:
- Use lifecycle.ignore_changes for ephemeral metadata used by the controller (e.g. last_boot_time).
- Separate "provisioning" and "runtime" statefiles/locks so accidental destroy doesn't remove runtime secrets.
- Emit a small checksum annotation on computed artifacts (e.g. template checksum) so controller can detect drift without destructive actions.

Bootstrap choreography (stepwise, with safety gates):
1) Preflight phase (Terraform-created resources validated):
   - Validate network routability (packets to api-lb, registry if not air-gapped), VLAN trunking, MTU tests.
   - Check ESXi host readiness (if vSphere): datastore free space, template checksum.
   - If ipxe: validate DHCP scope and TFTP reachability.
   - Emit preflight result JSON to resume_blob_uri.

2) Seed node provisioning (small control-plane subset):
   - Provision 1 (or 3) seed nodes depending on customer policy.
   - Controller waits for node to boot and for kubelet to register (kubelet bootstrap token exchange).
   - Run minimal control-plane health checks (etcd quorum, apiserver reachable, certificate bootstrap OK).
   - Gate: do not continue unless control-plane passes 3 successive health checks spaced 30s apart.

3) Incremental control-plane rollout:
   - Provision next batch of CP nodes, prefer canary if expected_control_plane_count > 3.
   - Each new CP join must pass health gate; if it fails, mark node as quarantined and fallback to previous known-good config.

4) Worker node join (parallel with throttling):
   - Join workers in small waves (configurable batch size), with node-level preflight: kubelet version match, container runtime ready, required kernel modules present.
   - If node fails health checks twice, place in 'rescue' flow (collect logs + preserve disk) and continue with next batch.

5) Post-join verification and soft-cutover:
   - Verify workload scheduling, verify default CNI routes, run a sample request against controlled test deployment to assert SLOs.
   - Capture telemetry snapshots (control-plane metrics, kubelet heartbeats) and store with resume_blob.

Upgrade strategy (control plane + kubelet) — non-blocking defaults:
- Control-plane upgrade path: canary-CP -> wait 5m -> 3 successive API health checks -> proceed. If API latency or errors increase above thresholds, automatic rollback of CP image is triggered (use templated vm images or rollback to previous machine image tag).
- Kubelet/node upgrade path: cordon -> drain with eviction-timeout override -> apply OS/kernel update -> reboot -> kubelet health check -> uncordon.
- If drain fails (pod disruption budget blocked), try: 1) increase grace period (temporary), 2) move to next node and retry later. Never drain more than N% concurrently (default 10%).

Rollback and data-preservation patterns:
- Always snapshot etcd before any CP upgrade if possible (or ensure remote etcd backup exists).
- When failing to join new CP node, do not destroy its volumes — snapshot and mark for later reprovisioning.
- For worker-level failure, keep disk attached and mark as salvageable; field kit can inspect.

Observability and telemetry (minimum):
- Health checks: kube-apiserver RPS & 5xx rate, etcd leader change counter, kubelet lastSeen, CRI restart counts.
- Bootstrap controller SHOULD emit step events to resume_blob and to a central aggregator (optional). Events: preflight, seed-provisioned, cp-join, worker-join, post-checks, upgrade-start, upgrade-end, rollback-start.
- Keep node boot logs (journald or console) for at least 72 hours by default; configurable via terraform var.

Field runbook snippets (quick commands):
- To re-run preflight locally (controller machine): ./bootstrap-controller --resume /mnt/resume/blob.json --verbose
- To inspect a node that failed join (via ipmi/console): journalctl -b -u kubelet -o short-precise
- To snapshot etcd (kubeadm/stacked etcd): ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snap.db --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/peer.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/peer.key

Risk matrix (short):
- Risk: Firmware/BIOS mismatch on baremetal -> Impact: boot failures -> Mitigation: preflight firmware checksum + automated firmware rollback option in template repo.
- Risk: DHCP scope exhaustion when ipxe-enabled -> Impact: nodes boot stuck -> Mitigation: allocate contingency IP pool and fail-fast check.
- Risk: Control-plane upgrade causes API latency spike -> Impact: reduced cluster availability -> Mitigation: canary CP with automatic rollback and pre-upgrade snapshot.

Open questions / TODOs (actionable):
- Decide on canonical resume_blob format (JSON schema v1) and publish schema to Confluence.
- Add terraform variable for "retain_failed_node_disk = true|false" default true for enterprise installs.
- Define exact thresholds for API latency / 5xx that should trigger CP rollback — proposal: 95th latency > 1s for 3 consecutive minutes or 5xx rate > 1% sustained for 2 minutes. Need SRE signoff.
- Explore optional lightweight node-side init (single small binary) for improved log shipping in air-gapped installs.

Appendix: example resume_blob (human readable sketch)
{
  "cluster": "acme-prod-23",
  "phase": "seed-join-complete",
  "seed_nodes": ["esxi-01", "esxi-02"],
  "last_event_ts": "2024-10-15T14:22:03Z",
  "preflight": {"network_ok": true, "tftp_ok": true},
  "control_plane_checksum": "sha256:..."
}

Notes-to-self / rough ideas:
- Keep the controller stateless where possible; use resume_blob and remote lock for leader election during field work.
- Try a "dry-run" terraform apply that only writes resume_blob without mutating provider resources for sensitive customer demos.

References and related docs:
- existing terraform modules repo (see linked PR)
- field install checklist (confluence)
- remote-logging design doc (confluence)

If you are reviewing: focus on terraform outputs shape, resume_blob schema, and the concrete health gate thresholds. I want a quick PR to the terraform modules repo that adds resume_blob_uri output and a "retain_failed_node_disk" variable.

-- Sofia
